title: Forwarded padded seam configuration
statement: Let $M$ be a family of six finite Boolean Turing machines, let $K\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $i\in\{0,1,2,3,4,5\}$ index a machine with positive work-tape count. For Boolean words $x,w,\mathrm{pre},\mathrm{out}$, a state $q$ of machine $i$, and an optional state $s$ of that machine, forwarding the configuration on input $x$ with optional state $s$, work-tape word $w$ on tape $0$ and all other work tapes blank, and output $\mathrm{out}$—padded to $K$ work tapes—gives the configuration on input $x$ with optional state mapped into the host state space (or the return state of module $i$ if $s$ is absent), work-tape word $w$ on tape $0$ and all other work tapes blank, and output $\mathrm{pre}\,\mathrm{out}$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a family of six finite Boolean Turing machines
$s$ is an optional state of machine $i$
replaced:
For a module with positive tape count: forwarding a padded canonical
configuration of the module (built from a state word, with a given output)
through the emitting embedding produces the host's canonical seam over the same
state word, with the supplied prefix prepended to the output; a halted module
state maps to the module's return state.
